answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it acts, a stake as heavy and unyielding as a ferrous anchor. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then demands a thousand real bonds, so the attacker drowns in an ocean of locked capital. Honest agents moor safely at the jetty and reclaim their bond through verified work, while sybils forfeit theirs on misbehavior, making fake identities economically pointless.
